q: Does the nu-VQE Jastrow non-unitary reweighting generalize cleanly to open-quantum-system (OQS) VQE, where the target is a non-equilibrium steady state of a Lindbladian rather than a Hamiltonian ground state?
basis: The paper frames J as a classical post-processing reweighting of a density matrix rho produced by a noisy quantum circuit; formally, Tr[JHJ rho]/Tr[J^2 rho] is well-defined for any positive rho, so nothing in the estimator forbids using it when rho is the steady state of a dissipative process rather than of unitary evolution + noise. But the paper does not test whether the Jastrow parameterization is expressive enough to compensate for structured dissipation (e.g. dephasing channels along non-Z axes) the way it compensates for depolarizing noise here.
next_steps: Reimplement the nu-VQE loop against a Qiskit / QuTiP Lindbladian steady-state solver for a small dissipative Bose-Hubbard or driven-dissipative TFIM. Compare the nu-VQE steady-state expectation of a local observable against exact vectorization of the Lindbladian. Sweep dissipation strength and check whether the same 10-30x error reduction holds, or whether the diagonal Jastrow is fundamentally limited to depolarizing / Z-basis noise.

q: How does nu-VQE compose with modern imaginary-time-evolution (ITE) variants (QITE, VarQITE, projected ITE) --- are they redundant, complementary, or does the non-unitary Jastrow act as a cheap surrogate for one ITE step?
basis: Both nu-VQE and QITE construct effectively non-unitary transformations of the ansatz state. QITE approximates exp(-tau H)|psi> with a compiled unitary (expensive: depth grows with tau); the nu-VQE Jastrow exp(sum alpha_k Z_k + sum alpha_kl Z_k Z_l) is diagonal and free at the circuit level but limited to a Z-basis product/pair structure. The paper does not compare wall-clock or accuracy per depth against QITE.
next_steps: On the same H2 / LiH 6-31G problem, run: (i) plain VQE, (ii) nu-VQE, (iii) 1-step VarQITE with matched circuit depth, (iv) nu-VQE seeded from a VarQITE-relaxed state. Report energy error vs total circuit depth and vs classical parameter count. This isolates whether the Jastrow does most of what one ITE step would do, at zero quantum cost.

q: Is the ~10-30x noise-error reduction robust to non-depolarizing noise channels --- specifically amplitude damping, coherent over-rotation, and correlated crosstalk --- or is it an artifact of the depolarizing / T1-T2 regime the paper tested?
basis: Depolarizing noise commutes with any J diagonal in the computational basis in a very clean way; amplitude damping does not (it breaks the population-preservation that the Jastrow reweighting implicitly assumes). Our replication used only depolarizing noise. The paper's ibmq_boeblingen model does contain amplitude damping but was not decomposed to isolate its contribution.
next_steps: Repeat the nu-VQE vs VQE comparison under four separately controlled channels: (a) pure depolarizing, (b) pure amplitude damping (T1-only), (c) coherent over-rotation of every Ry gate by a fixed epsilon, (d) correlated ZZ crosstalk on the CNOT. Report error-reduction ratio for each. If (b)-(d) show <2x reduction while (a) shows ~30x, the paper's claim is conditional on the noise-channel type, which is a material caveat.

q: Can an ML-selected / learned non-unitary structure outperform the hand-picked pairwise-Z Jastrow used in the paper, without inflating the classical parameter count?
basis: The paper picks J = exp(one-body Z + two-body ZZ) by chemistry intuition (Jastrow analogy from VMC). It is not shown that this is optimal, or even Pareto-optimal on the (accuracy, parameter-count) frontier. A learned structure (e.g. a small transformer or Gaussian-process meta-model that proposes which Pauli strings to include in J for a given Hamiltonian) could plausibly do better with fewer alpha parameters.
next_steps: Build a candidate library of J-generators up to weight 3 (Z, ZZ, XZ, XX, ZZZ, etc.), then use group-Lasso / L0-regularized optimization to prune to the smallest active set that hits chemical accuracy under a fixed noise model. Publish the Pareto curve of (nonzero alpha count) vs (energy error) and compare against the paper's default. If the diagonal-only J is Pareto-dominant, that is a positive robustness result; if a mixed X/Z J wins with fewer params, that is a strict improvement.

q: Does the nu-VQE formalism extend to non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonians --- e.g. PT-symmetric systems, resonance / Siegert-state calculations, or complex-scaled molecular Hamiltonians --- where standard VQE's variational principle breaks down?
basis: The estimator Tr[JHJ rho]/Tr[J^2 rho] is a Rayleigh-like quotient. For Hermitian H it is bounded below by the ground-state energy; for non-Hermitian H that bound does not hold and the optimization landscape becomes non-convex in a fundamentally different way. The paper deliberately restricts to Hermitian molecular H. Whether the non-unitary J can serve as a variational biorthogonal partner (left vs right eigenvector) for non-Hermitian problems is an open and potentially high-impact question.
next_steps: Take a small PT-symmetric 2-site Hatano-Nelson model (exactly solvable) and try three schemes: (i) standard VQE minimizing |<psi|H|psi>|^2, (ii) nu-VQE with J as defined by the paper, (iii) a biorthogonal ansatz (|psi_L>, |psi_R>) where J acts as an approximate similarity transform to make H look more Hermitian in the transformed basis. Compare against exact eigenvalues in both the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. If (ii) or (iii) reproduce the exceptional-point behavior, nu-VQE has a genuinely new application domain beyond ground-state chemistry.
